- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and forecast shows strong downward bias, increase forecast by 2–5% to avoid panic-driven undershoot.  
- If recent price action shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after spike), adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- If forecast overshoots true outcome by >3% after a spike, apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per subsequent day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term sentiment noise.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast in early days of the 30d window, assume model is overestimating momentum — apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 1–2% from forecast for days 1–5.
